# Tool surface — which tool is served where, and why

<!-- GENERATED by `npm run surface:build` from `src/tools/surface.ts`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Six mechanisms decide where a tool appears and two more decide whether the
call it receives there runs. Each is justified on its own terms and none is
collapsed into the others; this table is the single place that *joins* them,
so "why is tool X not on address Y" has one answer instead of six lists to
hold in your head.

It is computed from the running configuration — the same `decideView` that
builds every `tools/list` — and regenerated by `npm run surface:build`.
`src/tools/__tests__/surface-doc.test.ts` fails the build if this file and
the code disagree, which is how a surface change reaches a reviewer’s diff
(ADR-001 D4, D7).

`tools/list` bytes is the serialized result the view sends in the default
deployment — what a host that loads the whole list pays on every connection,
roughly 4 bytes per token. The budgets are in `src/tools/listing-budget.ts`;
the tests and `npm run surface:check` fail above them. `/mcp` is headed for
100,000 bytes or less by demotion and schema trims (ADR-001 D3).

A facet answers *how many tools fit in this host’s context*; `readonly`
answers *what may this agent do at all*. They are different kinds of view —
`readonly` is not a seventh facet (ADR-001 D3 addendum).

## Demoted from `/mcp`

Low-use groups served on their facet only (`-low` in the `/mcp` column).
The default view’s `initialize` instructions name each group and its address.

| Group | Served on | Tools |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the first-time setup wizard | `/mcp/onboarding` | `onboarding_add_categories`, `onboarding_add_positions`, `onboarding_add_services_batch`, `onboarding_add_team_members_batch`, `onboarding_create_test_appointments`, `onboarding_import_clients`, `onboarding_preview_data`, `onboarding_resume`, `onboarding_rollback_phase`, `onboarding_set_schedules`, `onboarding_start`, `onboarding_status` |
| event duplication patterns | `/mcp/ops` | `events_create_duplication_strategy`, `events_delete_duplication_strategy`, `events_list_duplication_strategies`, `events_update_duplication_strategy` |
| client files | `/mcp/ops` | `clients_list_files`, `clients_upload_file` |
| membership freeze, balance and validity changes | `/mcp/marketing` | `memberships_freeze`, `memberships_set_balance`, `memberships_set_validity`, `memberships_unfreeze` |
| archiving or deleting a membership type | `/mcp/marketing` | `memberships_archive_type`, `memberships_delete_type` |
| creating or deleting a booking form | `/mcp/catalog` | `booking_forms_create`, `booking_forms_delete` |

## Legend

| Code | Served? | Meaning | Declared in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | yes | the unfiltered view is never filtered | `ALL_TOOLS_FACET` |
| `base` | yes | every facet carries it unconditionally | `FACET_BASE_TOOLS` |
| `pwd!` | yes | admitted by the deployment switch | `PASSWORD_LOGIN_TOOLS` + `ALTEGIO_EXPOSE_PASSWORD_LOGIN` |
| `rule` | yes | named one by one in this facet | `FACET_RULES[<facet>].tools` |
| `pfx` | yes | matched by this facet’s prefix | `FACET_RULES[<facet>].prefixes` |
| `xtra` | yes | re-admitted to `/mcp` despite an excluded prefix | `DEFAULT_FACET_EXTRA_TOOLS` |
| `dflt` | yes | on `/mcp` because nothing excludes it | (the default) |
| `ro` | yes | declares `readOnlyHint: true` | the tool’s own annotations |
| `list` | yes | listed on `/mcp/compact`: the most used tools and the dispatcher | `COMPACT_VIEW_TOOLS`, `DISPATCH_TOOLS` |
| `disp` | through the dispatcher | not listed on `/mcp/compact`; `tools_search` finds it, `tools_call_read` / `tools_call_write` run it | `dispatchReaches` |
| `-pwd` | no | a password prompt under an OAuth endpoint | `PASSWORD_LOGIN_TOOLS` + `ALTEGIO_EXPOSE_PASSWORD_LOGIN` |
| `-name` | no | a dangerous right `/mcp` does not hand a generic agent | `DEFAULT_FACET_EXCLUDED_TOOLS` |
| `-pack` | no | a whole pack held back from `/mcp`’s byte budget | `DEFAULT_FACET_EXCLUDED_PREFIXES` |
| `-low` | no | a low-use group served on its facet only | `DEFAULT_FACET_DEMOTED_GROUPS` |
| `-` | no | this facet’s rule does not name it | `FACET_RULES[<facet>]` |
| `-write` | no | it changes data, so the read-only address will not serve it | the tool’s own annotations |
| `-cmp` | no | the dispatcher is listed on `/mcp/compact` only | `DISPATCH_TOOLS` |
| `-off` | no | withheld from every view, stdio included | `DISABLED_TOOL_NAMES` |

**A withheld tool is refused, not merely hidden.** What the caller
reads depends on why:

- `-off` — the tool is not registered at all, so the call answers `Unknown tool`.
- any code in the `/readonly` column — the read-only policy message, which names
  the full address of the complete surface and tells the model to report rather
  than retry.
- `disp` in the `/compact` column — not refused: the dispatcher runs it, and so
  does a direct call by name.
- every other column — the out-of-view error, naming the paths that do serve it
  (or saying the deployment serves it nowhere).

The **Gates** column applies wherever the tool is served: these refuse the call
after it is accepted, in the order `src/tools/registry.ts` checks them.

- a scope name — the caller’s token must carry it (`src/tools/scopes.ts`). A
  caller that declares no scopes, which is every deployment today, passes.
- `confirm` — a human approves it first, by elicitation or a one-time token bound
  to the exact arguments (`src/tools/confirmation.ts`).
- `reads-only` — the handler itself performs documented GETs only and refuses any
  other method (ADR-001 D2).

## Deployment switches

The table above describes the default configuration, password login off.
One environment switch changes it.

`ALTEGIO_EXPOSE_PASSWORD_LOGIN=true` (the closed staff deployment):

- `/mcp` — +`auth_login`, +`auth_logout`
- `/mcp/compact` — +`auth_login`, +`auth_logout`
- `/mcp/ops` — +`auth_login`, +`auth_logout`
- `/mcp/catalog` — +`auth_login`, +`auth_logout`
- `/mcp/finance` — +`auth_login`, +`auth_logout`
- `/mcp/marketing` — +`auth_login`, +`auth_logout`
- `/mcp/analytics` — +`auth_login`, +`auth_logout`
- `/mcp/onboarding` — +`auth_login`, +`auth_logout`
